On the chest radiograph, lobar hyperinflation of the right middle lobe with mediastinal shift to the left and concurrent atelectasis of the other lobes was observed (Figure 2). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial chest CT in a neonate demonstrates left upper lobe overinflation with low attenuation, contralateral mediastinal shift, and compression atelectasis, consistent with congenital lobar overinflation. B: Axial chest CT shows left upper lobe and right middle lobe hyperinflation with low attenuation, mediastinal shift, and adjacent lobe compression in congenital lobar overinflation. C: Axial chest CT at a lower level demonstrates overinflated low-attenuation lobes with compressive atelectasis/collapse of adjacent lobes and mediastinal shift, consistent with bilateral congenital lobar overinflation. D: Coronal CT minimum intensity projection shows overinflated low-attenuation lobes and collapsed adjacent lobes with mediastinal shift in a neonate with congenital lobar overinflation.
panels.attribution_text: Zinaye and Zeray. Bilateral congenital lobar overinflation (CLO) - a rare presentation of an uncommon condition.. Radiology case reports 2022. doi:10.1016/j.radcr.2022.07.020. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Axial chest CT images in lung window settings at different levels (A through C) demonstrate the presence of marked overinflation of the left upper lobe (arrows) resulting in compressive atelectasis of the left lower lobe (arrowhead) and significant mediastinal shift to the right. Right middle lobe hyperinflation (asterisk) with collapse consolidation of the right upper and lower lobes is also seen (C). Coronal minimal intensity projection (D) better demonstrates the overinflated and collapsed lobes.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Transverse fetal ultrasound shows an enlarged hyperechoic left upper lobe with pulmonary asymmetry, consistent with the caption-confirmed congenital lobar overinflation. b: Axial fetal T2 MRI demonstrates asymmetric lungs with an enlarged high-T2-signal left upper lobe, matching the caption diagnosis of congenital lobar overinflation. c: Sagittal fetal T2 MRI shows the enlarged, homogeneously high-signal left upper lobe described in the caption for congenital lobar overinflation. d: Sagittal chest CT at 6 months shows a hyperexpanded left upper lobe; the caption states surgery confirmed congenital lobar overinflation.
panels.attribution_text: Caro-Domínguez et al. Prenatal ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and therapeutic options for fetal thoracic anomalies: a pictorial essay.. Pediatric radiology 2023. doi:10.1007/s00247-023-05681-y. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 9.
panels.figure_caption: a–c Congenital lobar overinflation in a 29-week gestational age male fetus. Transverse ultrasound image (a) and axial (b) and sagittal (c) T2 single-shot magnetic resonance images (MRI) show asymmetry of the lungs; the left upper lobe is enlarged with hyperechogenicity on ultrasound and homogeneous high T2 signal on MRI. d A sagittal computed tomography image on lung window settings performed at 6 months of age demonstrates a hyperexpanded left upper lobe. Surgery two months later confirmed congenital lobar overinflation
in_text_mentions: erinflation is usually a homogeneous hyperechoic solid mass that may present with hypervascularity [38]. Fetal MRI shows an expanded homogeneously solid lesion with high T2 signal without cysts (Fig. 9) [8].
